w:r.w:t: Lab investigation report • Prepared from the supplied challenge evidence

A backend developer installed a malicious MCP integration after visiting http://awesomeawsmcp.com/ on 20 April 2026 at 20:57. The installer executed a payload hosted at http://3.72.63.40:80/payload/s.exe. The payload established command and control, began with the command “pwd,” and targeted AWS credentials. The attacker staged credentials in C:\Users\Administrator\.exfil\, then used the compromised IAM user admin to launch GPU-capable EC2 instances across four AWS regions. The instances were tagged prod-web-server and used type p3.2xlarge. The infrastructure connected to rx.unmineable.com:3333 to mine Solana. The associated wallet was later linked to the April 2026 Drift Protocol exploit.

The investigation reconstructs workstation compromise, credential access, cloud-account abuse, resource impact, and cryptocurrency mining activity. Evidence shown in the lab included browser history, MCP configuration, endpoint artifacts, CloudTrail logs, and blockchain explorer results.
20 Apr 2026 20:57 — Victim visited awesomeawsmcp.com. The site promoted an MCP server named AWS dev ops.
Shortly afterward — Cursor executed an embedded command and downloaded s.exe from 3.72.63.40.
Post-compromise — The attacker established C2, ran pwd, and targeted AWS credentials. Credentials were staged under C:\Users\Administrator\.exfil\.
Cloud abuse — AWS API calls came from 3.72.63.40 using InfrastructureAutomation/3.0.1 go1.22.5 (cloud-ops-deployment) linux/amd64 and the compromised principal arn:aws:iam::990227772331:user/admin.
Impact — 16 EC2 instances were launched across four regions, all tagged prod-web-server and using p3.2xlarge.
Mining — The recovered script connected to rx.unmineable.com:3333 and mined Solana. The vault-to-attacker transfer was 45,292.208963921 dSOL.

This was a supply-chain-style workstation compromise followed by cloud credential theft and resource hijacking. Recommended actions: revoke and rotate the compromised IAM credentials; preserve CloudTrail, endpoint, and browser evidence; terminate unauthorized instances; block the C2/mining indicators; review all regions for persistence; audit billing and IAM changes; and report the wallet and related transactions to the relevant exchange, protocol, and incident-response contacts.
